name: Marble House

dates.altered: A Chinese Tea House was added on the cliff in 1913-14 for Alva Belmont; the house has been a museum of the Preservation Society of Newport County since 1963.
dates.note: The style node's exemplar gives 1892, which is the completion date; Wikipedia's infobox gives 'Built 1888-92' and the National Trust's page 'built between 1888 and 1892'. No disagreement, so nothing is reconciled.

refs.title: Marble House - Wikipedia
refs.note: Gives the address as 596 Bellevue Avenue, the architect as Richard Morris Hunt, the style as 'Beaux Arts', and the temple-front portico compared to the White House's.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 71000025; added September 10, 1971; designated NHL February 17, 2006; contributing property of the Bellevue Avenue Historic District (ID72000023), as the Wikipedia infobox prints it
refs.note: Read from the infobox, not from the National Register's own database, which was not opened for this building.

refs.title: Designing Leisure in the Gilded Age - Material Matters (University of Delaware)
refs.note: UNRESOLVED, AND RECORDED AS SUCH. This page's caption reads 'Bellevue Avenue, Newport, Newport County, RI Photos from Survey HABS RI-330. Library of Congress', which is the only claim found that Marble House carries a HABS number. It was not confirmed against a Library item record or a data page, and no `survey` block is written on the strength of it. A HABS record of photographs alone carries no written data in any case.

note: Written for WP-11.2 Tranche 2, the French modes and the Beaux-Arts. Searched for a HABS survey on loc.gov, in Wikimedia Commons and against the getarchive/PICRYL index that carries survey numbers for Newport; the queries returned The Elms (RI-344), the Redwood Library (RI-100) and the Mary T. Porter House (RI-314) but no confirmable number for Marble House, so this record carries locators and no measurements. That is a complete record under the schema, not a gap in it.
